ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure is the graph of the function $y_{1}=|x|$. It is known that the graph of the function $y_{2}=\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{4}{3}$ intersects with the graph of $y_{1}=|x|$ at points A and B, and $A(-1, 1)$, then what is the range of values of $x$ for which $y_{2}>y_{1}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\
by solving the system of equations $\begin{cases}y=x \\ y=\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{4}{3}\end{cases}$, we get: $\begin{cases}x=2 \\ y=2\end{cases}$,\\
$\therefore$ Point B is (2, 2),\\
From the graph, it is found that when $y_{2}>y_{1}$, $-1<x<2$,\\
thus, the answer is: $x \in \boxed{(-1, 2)}$.

It is known that the graph of the function $y_{2}=\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{4}{3}$ intersects with the graph of $y_{1}=|x|$ at points A and B, and $A(-1, 1)$, then what is the range of values of $x$ for which $y_{2}>y_{1}$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\ by solving the system of equations $\begin{cases}y=x \\ y=\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{4}{3}\end{cases}$, we get: $\begin{cases}x=2 \\ y=2\end{cases}$,\\ $\therefore$ Point B is (2, 2),\\ From the graph, it is found that when $y_{2}>y_{1}$, $-1<x<2$,\\ thus, the answer is: $x \in \boxed{(-1, 2)}$.

The other intersection point B is on the right branch y1=x, so let x=(1/3)x+4/3, obtaining (2/3)x=4/3, so x=2, y=2, namely B=(2,2). The two images are equal at x=-1 and x=2; from the image relationship and the intersecting positions of the straight line and the V-shaped image, it can be known that the straight line y2 is above y1 between the two intersection points, and is equal at the endpoints. Therefore, the range of values of x for y2>y1 is -1<x<2.
